parts.note: REM is rapid eye movement, the deep dreaming stage of sleep; people who are short of it are those who cannot sleep, not fans of a band

explanation.surface: An exclamation about devoted fans of the band R.E.M.
explanation.walkthrough: The lower-case 'rem' tempts you towards the rock band; it is the sleep phase, so the people are poor sleepers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufferers from chronic sleeplessness never get enough deep dreaming sleep.

explanation.surface: A gambler who bets and loses everything, down to the shirt off their back.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'lose one's shirt' is to lose all one's money; read literally, someone shirtless is left standing 'in vest', in only their undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To put money into a venture is a speculative bet; and with the shirt gone a person is left wearing only an undershirt.

parts.note: an error or wrongdoing is a sin
terrible means bad

explanation.surface: A mistake made by an incompetent seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary seafarer of the Arabian Nights tales made seven voyages.

clue.text: Pinch young lady — not altogether proper

indicators.note: the word for the young lady is not given in full, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Miss is the title of a young unmarried lady
proper means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of pinching a young lady in a way that is not quite proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch' suggests a nip on the arm, but it means steal. 'not altogether' trims MISS to MIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is slang for to steal, which is to take dishonestly for one's own use.

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure and jumbled, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver admits defeat on a cryptic clue they cannot crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' rearranges CLUEICANT; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix an idea firmly in someone's mind is to instil it by repetition.

indicators.note: the word for speak goes around the letter for new

parts.note: to speak informally is to chat

explanation.surface: Newspeak, the Orwellian language, wrapped around a political slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New speak' looks like Orwell's Newspeak; it splits into N and a word for speak, with 'around' putting CHAT round the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A chant is a repeated phrase shouted by a crowd, much like a rallying cry.

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word for declared swap places

parts.note: declared means said

explanation.surface: A position stated openly, then reversed at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing ends' swaps the S and D of SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform on which a speaker or a top table stands.

clue.text: Showing skill, young Arthur is endlessly shown to be correct

parts.note: Art is a familiar short form of the name Arthur
taken as written

indicators.note: the word for the correct mark loses its last letter

parts.note: a tick marks something as correct

explanation.surface: A gifted child named Arthur is always being proved right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TICK to TIC; 'shown to be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Displaying flair and creative talent, as an artist does.

clue.text: Tory leader, for example, in abandoned policy

indicators.note: the letters for the Tory leader and for example go inside the word for abandoned

parts.note: an abandoned animal is a stray

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A Conservative party chief's plan is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like an anagram signal, but it gives STRAY; 'in' places T plus EG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is an overall plan of action, a course adopted to reach a goal.

clue.text: Its economy may be in immature hands!

definitions.text: Its economy may be in immature hands!

parts.words: Its economy may be in immature hands!
parts.note: the 'immature hands' are bunches of unripe fruit, which grow in hands, so this is a small state reliant on that single crop, and the phrase also mocks inexperienced rulers

explanation.surface: A warning that a country's finances are run by childish leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hand' is a bunch of bananas; the term is used for small, unstable states that depend on one export.
explanation.definitionFit: A derisive term for a politically unstable small country dependent on exporting one crop.

clue.text: Vision emerging naked — under sea, initially

definitions.text: Vision emerging naked — under sea, initially

indicators.note: the opening letters of the five words before it are taken in order

explanation.surface: Describes the famous painting of a goddess rising naked from the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is also the definition: Botticelli's goddess emerges naked from the sea on a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of love was born from sea foam, depicted rising nude from the waves.

clue.text: A Conservative in authority shows integrity

indicators.note: the A and C go inside the word for authority

parts.note: a charter is a document granting authority or rights

explanation.surface: A Tory in power demonstrates his honesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of good moral fibre and strong principles is said to have this quality.

clue.text: It's the cutting edge of the theatre

definitions.text: It's the cutting edge of the theatre

parts.words: It's the cutting edge of the theatre
parts.note: the theatre is an operating theatre, and the cutting edge is literally the blade a surgeon uses there, not the latest drama

explanation.surface: Praise for the most innovative work on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting edge' and 'theatre' suggest avant-garde drama; it is a surgeon's blade in the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, very sharp surgical knife used for incisions.

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the letter for new
something struggling is in disarray, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hard-up painter takes up a fresh artistic movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' rearranges ARTIST into TRASIT; 'embracing' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Passage or conveyance from one place to another, as in goods in transport.

indicators.note: the word for smashing lets the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: smashing means breaking

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unknown way of arranging, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word that, the 's being only a link

explanation.surface: Something smashing, it is admitted, and somehow stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges THAT into THTA; 'admitting' puts it inside BREAKING after BREA.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishing enough to make one gasp, so awe-inspiring.

clue.text: Showing no emotion, the man's innocent

parts.note: the man is he; the 's is read as is, linking the pieces
artless means innocent and without guile

explanation.surface: A man declared blameless despite seeming cold and unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking compassion or feeling, cold and unkind.

indicators.note: the word for fast holds the shortened word inside it

parts.note: fast, as in held fast, means tight

indicators.note: the word for testament loses its last letter

parts.note: a last will and testament

explanation.surface: Someone on their deathbed rushes to finish writing their will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts WILL to WIL; 'holding' places it inside TIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, as in one's last years of life, it means waning or in decline.

indicators.note: the letters for the gas go around the word for final

parts.note: CS gas is the tear gas used by riot police
latter means the last or final one

explanation.surface: Police fire tear gas to end the last of the industrial strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' looks like industrial action, but it is a verb: hits with a loud rattling noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Hits noisily, making a rattling or banging sound.

clue.text: Ordered fine paper, possibly, with socialist following

parts.note: fine means well, as in feeling well

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Someone orders good-quality paper, and a left-winger follows suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges PAPER into PREPA; 'with ... following' only places RED last.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in good order and readiness in advance.

indicators.note: the shortened word wears, or goes around, the word for party
the word for wild loses its last letter

parts.note: feral means wild, as of an animal
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party-goer wears an endlessly wild hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts FERAL to FERA; 'wearing' puts DO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft felt hat with a brim and a lengthwise crease in the crown.

clue.text: Leak from head of state in peace process

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the rearranged letters
processing changes something's form, so the letters are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A head of state leaks information during peace negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' rearranges PEACE to ECAPE; 'in' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas or liquid getting out through a hole is an outflow from a container.

clue.text: Bugs circling a taut, empty web

indicators.note: the word for bugs goes around the other letters

parts.note: lice are bugs

indicators.note: the word taut is emptied of its middle letters, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Insects crawl round a tight, empty web.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves TT from 'taut'; 'circling' puts A plus TT inside LICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A criss-cross framework of strips, like a mesh or net.

clue.text: Muse in production by hera? Tosh!

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the letters produced by the next words

explanation.surface: A muse appears in a dismissive review of a show by Hera.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'hERA TOsh' across the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one presiding over love poetry.

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient's muscles stiffen as lockjaw sets in.
explanation.definitionFit: Draws tight, making something taut and rigid.

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince is said to be occasionally mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is a celebrated Danish prince; the other reading is a large breed of dog, and 'barking' is also British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince of Denmark is a notable man from Denmark; a big dog breed sometimes barks.

indicators.note: back means the A and the word for kid are read backwards together

parts.note: to kid is to fool; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A child's back is washed with a sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AFOOL round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried gourd skin used as a rough bath scrubber.

indicators.note: the letters for question and time are put into a new order

parts.note: to question is to ask

explanation.surface: The Labour party reschedules question time in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party but is plain work; 'reordered' puts T ahead of ASK.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work or a job to be done.

clue.text: Set aside cheats with European commission payment

parts.note: cons are swindles or cheats
a rate is a charge or payment

explanation.surface: A fraudster's fees from a Brussels body are put to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To dedicate something to sacred use is to reserve it for a holy purpose.
